title: BMZ -- EAC AI Alliance regional AI research and training network
description: "THE German government has committed euros 5m to the East African Community (EAC) to set up a regional artificial intelligence (AI) research and training network... the funding will support the formulation and rollout of an EAC AI strategy for 2025 to 2028, along with equipping 50,000 young people across partner states with cutting-edge digital skills." Includes USD50,000 in prize funding for the AI4EAC Innovation Challenge's second edition (per the EAC's own 12 August 2026 release, raw/2026/2026-08-12-bmz-eac-ai4eac-innovation-challenge.md), which also names new partners Equity Group Holdings and the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) and introduces an Ebola Response Challenge track. The 2025 pilot mobilised 3,891 (per EAC) / 3,900 (per this source) students across ~57-100 universities in Burundi, DRC, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania and Uganda.
recipient_organisation: East African Community (EAC Secretariat, implemented by GIZ with IUCEA and EASTECO)

title: Axian Telecom (Yas) Acquisition of Wananchi Group \u2014 Zuku/Simbanet
description:
On 5–7 November 2025, Axian Telecom Fibre Ltd (trading as Yas) completed the acquisition of 99.63% of Wananchi Group Holdings Ltd for approximately USD 63 million (KES 9.6 billion). Wananchi Group operates Zuku (consumer broadband/IPTV, Kenya) and Simbanet (enterprise connectivity, Tanzania). The acquisition extends Axian's fixed broadband footprint into Kenya, Tanzania (integrated with existing Yas Tanzania) and Uganda. The deal was partly financed by the USD 600M 2025 bond (part of proceeds) and separately by an IFC loan of USD 25M plus USD 37.5M from partner lenders.

Recipient countries: KEN, UGA.

title: Vodacom Group — Safaricom controlling stake, 2025
description:
"Pan-African telecoms operator Vodacom Group has announced a $2.1 billion deal that will see it increase its stake in Kenya's Safaricom to 55%. Under the terms of the deal, Vodacom has entered into an agreement with the Government of Kenya to acquire 15% of Safaricom PLC and an additional 5% from Vodafone at 34 Kenyan shillings (US$0.26) per share, valuing the deal at $2.1 billion." The transaction requires regulatory and governmental approvals in Kenya, Ethiopia and South Africa; Kenya retains a 20% stake and board representation.

Recipient countries: KEN, ETH.
